newsitem.title: USA: Cypress sees positive results from trial.
newsitem.headline: Cypress sees positive results from trial.

text.p: Cypress Bioscience Inc Wednesday announced positive results in its clinical trial for Infusible Platelet Membranes (IPM) in halting active bleeding.

In a statement, the company said the Phase II trial, which began a year ago, was designed to study efficacy in patients with low platelet counts during active bleeding episodes. The study showed that IPM controlled or halted bleeding in 17 of 26 patients, a 65 percent response rate.

Cypress said 12 of the 26 patients had previously not responded to platelet transfusions, the traditional therapy for uncontrolled bleeding. In this subgroup of nonresponders, IPM was effective in controlling or halting bleeding in seven out of 12 patients, or 58 percent of the time, the company said.

Cypress had originally planned to study 36 patients, but because of the positive results, the company said the trial was halted at 31 patients so it could begin a Phase II dose-ranging study. The dose-ranging study, which will commence shortly, must be conducted before launching the pivotal Phase III trial, it added.
The Phase II trial was conducted in 31 patients at seven sites. The company said the safety profile of the product continues to be favorable without any reportable adverse effects.
Cypress develops, manufactures and markets medical devices and therapeutics for the treatment of certain types of immune disorders.
